data.name: Jwala
data.gender_notes: Jwala is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Jwala is derived from the Sanskrit word ‘jvala’, which means ‘a wick’, ‘a torch’, or ‘a flame’. In Hindu mythology, Jwala is the name of the Goddess of Fire, Agni. She is depicted as a fiery being with the power to consume all evil and purify the soul. The name Jwala carries the meaning “Goddess of Fire” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Jwala usually hope their child will grow to embody goddess of fire and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the inner fire of passion, love, and determination.
data.etymology: Jwala belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Goddess of Fire.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Jwala total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.
